cobra-hpca2022-paper.title: Improving Locality of Irregular Updates with Hardware Assisted Propagation Blocking
cobra-hpca2022-paper.edition: HPCA 2022 author-hosted 15-page paper; publisher-byte identity not established
cobra-hpca2022-paper.locator_basis: One-based PDF pages; sections, figures, tables and algorithms. Proceedings pp. 543–557.

cobra-phase-boundary.statement: PB materializes index/value tuples during Binning, then software Accumulate reads bins and applies destination updates. Neighbor-Populate bins (e.src,e.dst); Algorithm 2 partitions bins across Accumulate workers and uses ordinary Add on offsets, whereas Algorithm 1 uses AtomicAdd. Unordered neighbor lists permit the changed order.
limitations: No general permission to reorder noncommutative operations or floating-point arithmetic; no hardware destination update/atomic executor.

cobra-hierarchy.statement: Hardware-managed per-level cacheline C-Buffers collect tuples over progressively narrower index ranges; full L1/L2 buffers are unpacked and repartitioned into next-level C-Buffers; full LLC buffers go to per-thread memory bins. This combines inexpensive small-buffer-set Binning with many bins for Accumulate.
limitations: Coalescing here means tuple collection, not same-index arithmetic reduction.

cobra-init.statement: bininit operands are cache-level identifier, number of reserved ways, number of unique indices, and tuple size in bytes. It reserves ways, computes the smallest power-of-two bin range whose C-Buffers fit, stores the range, and records actually used ways so unused reserved capacity can be reclaimed.
limitations: No encoding, header, C prototype, error convention or complete legal configuration interval is specified.

cobra-insert.statement: binupdate takes an index and update value and appends that pair to the selected L1 C-Buffer. Index high bits select buffer/set/way after removing log2(bin range) low bits. Per-buffer counters select the next tuple slot and wrap when full. C-Buffers are not byte addressable and exist outside shared-memory address space.
limitations: The supplied index selects a partition, not a direct store to the application destination address. No old destination value is returned by this collection contract.

cobra-private-metadata.statement: C-Buffers and bins are duplicated per thread; cache C-Buffers are core-private. Replacement/dirty/coherence bits can be repurposed for tuple counters. LLC banks are divided among cores; per-core LLC buffer count is bounded by the assigned bank capacity. LLC tags store per-bin offsets.
limitations: Private buffer metadata reuse does not establish coherent observer visibility of final application updates.

cobra-drain.locator: PDF p. 7, §V.D, Fig. 8; PDF p. 11, §VII.B, Fig. 13a
cobra-drain.statement: A full C-Buffer transfers as a cacheline to a FIFO eviction buffer; the binning engine later sequentially extracts and serially inserts tuples into next-level buffers using that level’s range. Buffer sizing uses Little’s Law then a burst-aware DES model; full eviction buffers can stall Binning.
limitations: No complete queue-credit reservation, cross-level arbitration, deadlock/progress proof, or packet acknowledgment protocol is provided.

cobra-memory-bins.statement: Each thread has contiguous tuples per bin with precomputed counts and starting BinOffset entries. An unnamed ISA instruction initializes LLC tag offsets from buffer ID and starting offset. A full LLC buffer writes to BinBasePtr + BinOffset[binID], advances the offset by its tuple count, and resets its counter.
limitations: The text alternates pointer/offset and tuple-count descriptions; physical byte scaling and register binding are not a specified ABI. Bin base initialization and the unnamed instruction’s encoding remain unknown.

cobra-flush.locator: PDF p. 8, §V.E, Flushing the Cache After Binning
cobra-flush.statement: binflush marks end of Binning. Each core walks nonempty C-Buffers serially, L1 then L2 then its LLC bank, writing residual tuples to memory; eviction buffers, binning engines and offset logic must handle partial lines using tuple counters. All remaining tuples must reach bins before Accumulate.
limitations: Paper states the phase requirement, but does not specify a software-visible done/ack event, inter-core join, memory ordering/fence semantics, cancellation, or global write completion. binupdate retirement alone cannot release Accumulate.

cobra-os.locator: PDF p. 8, §V.E, Evicting from LLC / Handling virtualization / Need for Static Cache Partitioning
cobra-os.statement: The no-translation path assumes system support for matching virtual and physical addresses of important structures such as bins. Per-process way partitioning pins C-Buffers during Binning; other processes can evict partial buffers on preemption. Swapping a bin page invokes binflush; locking critical pages with mlock can avoid premature flush. A non-partitioned replacement-policy variant is evaluated separately.
limitations: mlock does not by itself establish matching VA/PA. No implemented kernel support, process isolation, migration/state-save protocol, translation-fault retry, or portable OS integration is verified.

cobra-issue.statement: The modified Sniper model makes binupdate retire only at the ROB head because it writes data caches like a store; operand-selected C-Buffers avoid the usual address-generation port. CACTI supplies cache timings; a custom Pin cache simulator models selected studies.
limitations: Reported modeling is not inspected runnable source or a guarantee of global visibility on retirement.

cobra-parameters.locator: PDF p. 6, §V.A; p. 7, §V.C–D; p. 9, §VI/Table II; p. 11, §VII.B/Fig. 13
cobra-parameters.statement: Reference hierarchy: 16 OoO cores, 2.66 GHz, 4-wide issue, 128 ROB, 48 load and 32 store queue entries; 32 KB 8-way L1, 256 KB 8-way L2, 2 MB/core 16-way LLC. Default reserves all but one L1/LLC way and one L2 way with stream prefetching. 64 B line and 8 B tuple illustrate eight tuple slots. DES motivates 32-entry L1→L2 eviction buffering, while the L2→LLC Little’s Law estimate is one entry.
limitations: These are paper settings/examples, not portable legal ranges. The paper’s 4/8/16 B workload tuples do not establish arbitrary payload types or index-width support.

cobra-bottleneck.statement: Software PB trades fewer bins for cheap Binning against more bins for cache-local Accumulate. Many software C-Buffers and their management instructions/branches limit Binning. Hierarchical hardware buffering removes this compromise; eviction bursts and capacity retained for prefetched non-buffer data remain limiting factors.
limitations: No DX100 speedup, workload suitability or measured producer/consumer balance follows from the paper.

cobra-comm-exclusion.statement: COBRA-COMM is a separate commutativity-specialized design with LLC same-index tuple reduction and an atomic LLC reduction unit enabling shared LLC buffers.
limitations: Excluded from this base COBRA mapping; its reduction unit cannot be inherited by base COBRA.

mechanism_families.description: Cacheline tuple collection and hierarchical repartitioning for software propagation blocking; no inherited atomics.

designs.name: COBRA HPCA 2022 required tuple-binning mapping
designs.summary: Hardware collects and repartitions supplied tuples into per-thread bins for software PB Accumulate.

result.form: Partitioned per-thread index/value tuple sequences in memory bins; no destination-array update.
result.validity: All submitted tuples must reach their assigned bins before CPU Accumulate; requires counts/capacity, ownership and phase-release obligations.

ordering.scope: Thread-private collection and later bin traversal
ordering.description: Append slots preserve index/value association and tuple multiplicity. Hierarchical repartitioning and cross-thread/bin traversal do not establish original global update order or stable sorting.

completion.event: binflush initiates per-core L1→L2→LLC residual drain at the Binning boundary; physical done/ack binding unspecified.
completion.visibility: Paper requires all tuples in memory bins before Accumulate; ROB retirement is not bin drain, destination update completion, or a global write barrier.

operations.datatype_notes: Neighbor-Populate evaluation uses 8 B tuples; no supported catalog payload type or index-width domain inferred from this size. Index/value pair is data to collect.
limitations: Required program write is tuple materialization, not arbitrary scatter or atomic destination update.
No byte-address pattern coverage established for C-Buffers.
No observed executable model or ISA implementation.

realization.description: bininit per level; initialize per-bin LLC offsets with unnamed instruction; binupdate(index,value) per tuple; binflush then externally bound phase release. Paper interface description only.

requirements.description: Prove reordered bin processing preserves the application’s required outputs; Neighbor-Populate permits neighbor order variation. Preserve every tuple, including multiplicity.
Establish allowable floating-point order, integer overflow and any exact reproducibility obligations for the chosen application; commutativity is insufficient for bit-identical FP output.
Provide disjoint per-thread bin allocations and C-Buffer ownership; partition Accumulate destinations by bin or establish equivalent safe synchronization.

Compute per-thread/per-bin tuple counts and starting offsets before Binning; allocate sufficient contiguous capacity, keep namespace membership and offset arithmetic within allocations, and preserve pointer lifetime through drain/Accumulate.
Configure each cache level and its actually used ways; verify C-Buffers fit and per-core LLC bank assignments. This mapping selects the partitioned base design, not the unpinned variant.
Supply the assumed matching VA/PA support for bins and coordinate paging; page locking alone is not this mapping.

Establish all producers have stopped, all levels/eviction queues and outstanding bin writes have drained, and required consumer visibility before starting CPU Accumulate. The paper does not give the physical completion/ack/fence binding.
Bind process/thread/core ownership across preemption, page eviction and migration; retain offsets and partial tuple counts safely.
Bind queue-full backpressure, downstream service and partial-flush admission so buffered tuples cannot be overwritten or lost; no credit or deadlock protocol is claimed.
Recover bin-base setup, unnamed offset-init instruction and exact operand units/types/encoding before writing an executable wrapper.

interface.software_supplies: Index/value tuples, per-level configuration, precomputed per-thread bin capacities/base/offsets, ownership and assumed OS address support.
interface.invocation: Paper instructions bininit, binupdate, binflush plus unnamed LLC offset initializer. No C ABI or encoded ISA specification is proposed.
interface.outputs: Materialized tuple bins for software Accumulate. Software applies destination updates and supplies application-specific synchronization and numeric legality.

limitations: Production admission is pending parent review; this file is only an in-memory proposal.
C-Buffers are outside shared-memory address space; final bin-write acknowledgment and consumer fence are unresolved.
Base COBRA only; COBRA-COMM and non-partitioned variant excluded.
Paper specifications and model reports do not certify runnable hardware, mapping legality, numeric correctness or performance.

internal_mechanisms.description: Hardware-managed per-level cacheline C-Buffers collect tuples over progressively narrower index ranges; full L1/L2 buffers are unpacked and repartitioned into next-level C-Buffers; full LLC buffers go to per-thread memory bins. This combines inexpensive small-buffer-set Binning with many bins for Accumulate.

A full C-Buffer transfers as a cacheline to a FIFO eviction buffer; the binning engine later sequentially extracts and serially inserts tuples into next-level buffers using that level’s range. Buffer sizing uses Little’s Law then a burst-aware DES model; full eviction buffers can stall Binning.

The modified Sniper model makes binupdate retire only at the ROB head because it writes data caches like a store; operand-selected C-Buffers avoid the usual address-generation port. CACTI supplies cache timings; a custom Pin cache simulator models selected studies.

binflush marks end of Binning. Each core walks nonempty C-Buffers serially, L1 then L2 then its LLC bank, writing residual tuples to memory; eviction buffers, binning engines and offset logic must handle partial lines using tuple counters. All remaining tuples must reach bins before Accumulate.

performance_hypotheses.description: Hardware buffering may lower tuple-materialization latency when software buffer locality and management instructions dominate.
workload_conditions: Reordering is legal and tuple materialization is required.
Accumulate locality benefits from enough bins.
limiting_factors: Preprocessing counts/offsets and bin memory traffic
Prefetched-data capacity and CPU Accumulate time
